transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I conducted your post-cataract surgery follow-up check, and I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: According to the information I have, you should be able to start light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's always best to be gentle and avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous activities. Also, remember to wear protective eyewear when gardening.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thank you for that information! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know, thanks! I'm also finding that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. But if it's significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. If it's just mild, you can try wearing sunglasses when you're going outside.
